newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's PCS officially starts up new cracker.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's PCS officially starts up new cracker.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) said on Tuesday it has started up its new world-scale ethylene cracker with a 515,000-tonne-per-year capacity over the weekend.
The start up of the cracker or PCS II is as scheduled and on specification material, the company said in a statement.
Before this, a company spokeswoman had said that PCS was in the process of starting up the cracker on April 9.
The new cracker will double PCS's existing capacity to around one million tonnes per year, making it one of the largest olefins producers in the region.
PCS II is part of the Singapore $3.4-billion ($2.36 billion) expansion project of the Singapore Petrochemical Complex on Pulau Ayer Merbau and Pulau Seraya, two islands off southwestern Singapore.

PCS is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a consortium of Japanese companies comprising the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund, Sumitomo Chemicals 4008.3 and 33 other Japanese companies.
The company said the cracker is to meet the fast growing demand for petrochemical products in the region.

Late last year, managing director Takayuki Okada told Reuters that 80-percent of the naphtha feedstock required for the new plant had been secured on term basis, with 10-percent from the Middle East and the remainder from Singapore.
The new plant will more than double PCS's annual naphtha demand to 2.5 million tonnes (62,000 barrels-per-day) from around one million.
